title: Midwest Health - Security & KMS Review
summary: Discovery focused on security posture needs for a regulated healthcare customer. Main topics: SOC 2 / ISO requirements, SSO/SAML and RBAC, KMS integration and envelope encryption, audit logs retention, and options between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments. Action items agreed: Jordan to share SOC 2 report and architecture diagram; Priya to schedule a technical deep dive for KMS and audit log retention; customer to provide their compliance checklist. Next step is a security deep-dive and pricing for Dedicated capacity pilot.

transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we got about 45 minutes on the calendar, quick intros?
[00:08] Ben (Midwest Health - Head of Security): Ben Harper, head of security at Midwest Health. We're mainly trying to vet the security posture for any LLM vendor we bring into PHI workflows.
[00:16] Sara (CTO): Sara Liu here, overseeing infra and platform decisions.
[00:20] Carlos (Platform): Carlos Vega, I manage our cloud ops and kms.
[00:24] Jordan (Redwood): Great, I'm Jordan AE, and Priya our SE will cover the tech details.
[00:28] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all, thanks. Quick agenda: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML and RBAC, audit logs, KMS/encryption, deployment options.
[00:35] Ben: Our compliance team wants SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 mapped controls, and an explanation of how you handle keys and audit trails.
[00:42] Jordan: Absolutely, we can share our SOC2 report and control mapping. We also have an ISO gap document. Priya will go over KMS stuff.
[00:49] Priya: On KMS we support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we offer CMKs with envelope encryption and you can bring your own key via an external KMS either through a trust broker or direct HSM integration depending on the deployment.
[00:58] Carlos: Wait, for Hosted you said BYOK? How does network access to the KMS work? We are a VPC customer.
[01:04] Priya: For Hosted we do a broker pattern: key material stays in your KMS, we never persist raw keys. We use short-lived wrapping keys and envelope encryption; the actual unwrapping happens in a transient runner inside the private subnet. If you need full isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private with a direct VPC peering and customer-managed KMS endpoints.
[01:18] Sara: How about HSM / FIPS 140-2? Our procurement insists on HSM-backed keys for production PHI workloads.
[01:24] Priya: We integrate with major cloud HSM providers (AWS CloudHSM, Google HSM) and can support customer HSMs in Private deployment. For Hosted we rely on cloud HSMs and provide an attestation document. We'll surface the exact FIPS statements in the SOC artifacts.
[01:36] Ben: Auditability is big for us — immutable logs, retention policy, and log forwarding into our Splunk instance. How granular are the logs?
[01:44] Priya: We capture token-level request metadata, model variant, user id, route, and success/failure codes. We can export logs via syslog/forwarder or S3 exports with object locks for immutability. Retention is configurable per contract.
[01:56] Carlos: Is there PII or PHI in the logs? We can't have raw prompts retained longer than N days.
[02:02] Priya: By default logs include metadata only — we do not persist full prompts unless you opt-in for debugging and then it's scoped and TTL'd. For PHI workflows we recommend redaction at the edge or using in-flight tokenization and prefix caching to avoid storing prompts. We support configurable retention windows and automatic deletion hooks.
[02:18] Ben: Good — also need RBAC integration with our identity provider. SAML or SCIM?
[02:23] Jordan: We support SAML SSO for our Console and SCIM for provisioning. For API access we do token-based with short-lived tokens and optional session scoping.
[02:31] Sara: How are roles structured? We have legal, dev, ops, product — need fine-grained RBAC.
[02:35] Priya: We offer RBAC with role templates and granular permissions for model deploy, route config, and billing. You can map SAML groups to Redwood roles and enforce MFA and session limits.
[02:43] Ben: Is there an audit trail of role changes? We need to show who changed what in the console.
[02:47] Priya: Yes, console actions, API key creation, role changes—everything is logged with actor, timestamp, and IP. Logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[02:54] Carlos: From a networking point of view — if we go Dedicated, does Redwood manage the GPUs or we bring our own machines?
[03:00] Jordan: Dedicated is hosted by Redwood in our cloud but isolated from other tenants — you get reserved GPU pools, private VPC connectors, and the option for customer-managed KMS. If you need on-prem hardware we offer Private deployments as a package.
[03:11] Sara: Latency is a concern for inference. If we put it in a separate VPC will cross-region hops add too much latency?
[03:16] Priya: We can colocate Dedicated in the same region/az as your services and tune batching/kv cache to meet latency SLOs. We'll provide performance profiles per model so you can estimate p99 latency.
[03:26] Ben: For procurement: we need the SOC2 report, pen test summary, encryption detail, and a data processing addendum (DPA). Also want a sample contract redline.
[03:34] Jordan: We'll attach SOC2 Type II, recent pentest summary, DPA template, and a compliance matrix showing control mappings. Expect those in an email after the call.
[03:41] Carlos: One more thing around keys: do you rotate wrapping keys automatically?
[03:44] Priya: Yes wrapping keys rotated regularly; for BYOK you keep rotation control but we support automatic scheduled rotation if you allow. For Private we can tie into your HSM rotation policies.
[03:53] Ben: Any certifications around data residency? We host in us-central, but some patients are in other regions.
[03:58] Priya: We have region-specific hosting; for strict residency we recommend Private or Dedicated pinned to a region and we can provide attestations.
[04:06] Sara: On the legal side, any limits on token retention that you can put in contract?
[04:10] Jordan: Yes we can contractually cap retention windows and commit to automatic purge — we'll work with legal on DPA clauses.
[04:16] Ben: Alright, sounds promising. Could you walk briefly through a failure mode: say a key compromise — what's the incident playbook?
[04:23] Priya: If a key compromise is suspected we immediately revoke affected keys, rotate wrapping keys, terminate active sessions, and invalidate cached prefixes. We also provide incident reports, forensic logs, and help coordinate key rotation with your team. We run tabletop exercises for enterprise customers as part of onboarding.
[04:36] Carlos: How long do you retain KV cache and can we configure TTL to zero?
[04:40] Priya: KV cache TTLs are configurable; for PHI workloads we can disable persistent cache and set very short TTLs. It's a tradeoff with cost/latency but doable.
[04:48] Ben: Ok next steps then—send docs, schedule KMS deep-dive, and we'll loop in procurement.
[04:53] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and set the deep dive.
[04:57] Sara: Thanks, talk soon.
[04:59] (call ends)
notes: Priya suggested envelope encryption and broker pattern for Hosted BYOK
